method: Adds the dimensions of an assembly chain as a tolerance stack. Each dimension is a nominal value with a symmetric plus-or-minus tolerance and a direction: an adding dimension enters the total with a plus sign, a subtracting dimension (a bore, a spacer that closes a gap, a cover thickness) with a minus sign. The nominal total is the signed sum of the nominals. The worst-case total is that nominal less and plus the arithmetic sum of the tolerance magnitudes, T_wc = sum of t_i, which is the extreme reached when every dimension sits at a limit in the least favourable direction. The statistical total uses the root-sum-square of the same magnitudes, T_rss = sqrt(sum of t_i squared), which assumes the individual errors are independent, centred on nominal and approximately normal; it needs a real process behind it (inspected samples, a capable supplier or a control plan) and should not be used to excuse a stack that fails at worst case on a safety-relevant fit. Each dimension also reports its share of the worst-case range, t_i / T_wc, and of the total variance, t_i squared over the sum of squares, so the dominant contributor is visible. Optional lower and upper limits for the total are checked against both bands, and the result is reported dimension by dimension and as a total. Units are labels only: the arithmetic never converts between millimetres and inches, so every input must be in the same unit.
